content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Define isotopes and explain how they differ
Calculate the number of subatomic particles in isotopes
Explain why isotopes have the same chemical properties
Calculate relative atomic mass from isotope data
Give examples of isotopes and their uses
Atoms of the same element are not always identical. While all atoms of an element have the same number of protons, they can have different numbers of neutrons. These variants are called
are atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Carbon has three naturally occurring isotopes:
All three are carbon atoms (6 protons each), but they have different masses.
Chemical properties depend on electron arrangement, and isotopes have the same number of electrons (same as protons).
Because most elements exist as mixtures of isotopes, we use
- a weighted average of the masses of all isotopes.
This is why relative atomic masses in the Periodic Table are not whole numbers.
Chlorine has two isotopes: $^{35}\text{Cl}$ (75% abundance) and $^{37}\text{Cl}$ (25% abundance). Calculate the relative atomic mass of chlorine.
The relative atomic mass of chlorine is 35.5
Copper has two isotopes: $^{63}\text{Cu}$ and $^{65}\text{Cu}$. The relative atomic mass of copper is 63.5. Calculate the percentage abundance of each isotope.
Let x = percentage of $^{63}\text{Cu}$ Then (100 - x) = percentage of $^{65}\text{Cu}$

Hydrogen has three isotopes: $^{1}_1\text{H}$, $^{2}_1\text{H}$, and $^{3}_1\text{H}$. State the number of protons and neutrons in each isotope. (3 marks)
Explain why isotopes of the same element have identical chemical properties but different physical properties. (4 marks)
Boron has two isotopes: $^{10}\text{B}$ (20% abundance) and $^{11}\text{B}$ (80% abundance). Calculate the relative atomic mass of boron. (3 marks)
The relative atomic mass of bromine is 79.9. Bromine has two isotopes: $^{79}\text{Br}$ and $^{81}\text{Br}$. Calculate the percentage abundance of each isotope. (4 marks)
